Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
task_brief: Day 8 of "Junior Portfolio, Documentation, and Rights Review" (unit 6, grade 11) is a varied re-practice on junior portfolio, documentation, and rights review. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 45–75 minutes. The unit is working toward: Complete a junior portfolio with documentation standards, a rights review, and a capstone-year proposal. Today's work contributes to that by handling junior portfolio, documentation, and rights review at the reteach and varied practice stage, against the unit's wider topics of portfolio narrative and selection, high-quality documentation of work, artist statement and process writing, and copyright licensing and permissions review. This session is formative: it is scored on completeness and honesty of the record, not on getting a polished result.
primary_task: Return to junior portfolio, documentation, and rights review using a different medium or approach than your last attempt — if you worked visually, try it structurally or in writing; if you worked by ear, try it on paper. Make three short varied studies, spaced rather than all at once, and write after each what this approach made clear that the previous one did not. This work is not graded for quality; it is checked for whether your understanding of junior portfolio, documentation, and rights review now holds up in more than one form. Keep it private. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about junior portfolio, documentation, and rights review, and it belongs to "Junior Portfolio, Documentation, and Rights Review", which also covers separate topics such as portfolio narrative and selection. Close out with this check before you stop: Explain what the new representation of junior portfolio, documentation, and rights review made visible that the earlier one did not. At grade 11 the bar is independent work with sustained self-direction: you set the constraint, defend it, and revise on the evidence of your own checks rather than on being told to.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
task_accessibility_provisions: Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Public performance is never required. A private, low-audience, or written-and-scored alternative always carries the same academic target.
No recording of the learner’s voice, no photograph, and no video is ever required; documentation may be written, notated, sketched, or adult-verified instead.
Use only original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved works. Do not reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or other protected works without documented rights.
The tutor may explain technique, ask diagnostic questions, and critique work, but never silently completes graded creative work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, score excerpt, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting junior portfolio, documentation, and rights review.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or concrete model, or adult demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for junior portfolio, documentation, and rights review follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for junior portfolio, documentation, and rights review, model it in a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the approach to junior portfolio, documentation, and rights review works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of junior portfolio, documentation, and rights review, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "requests the answer to graded work": Explain the concept, ask a diagnostic question, or help isolate the defect. Do not supply the graded artifact, solution code, or finished creative work. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking junior portfolio, documentation, and rights review mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply junior portfolio, documentation, and rights review under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on junior portfolio, documentation, and rights review rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
